An n by n matrix A is diagonalizable over F exactly when F^n has a basis of eigenvectors of A.
Distinct eigenvalues have independent eigenvectors. A real symmetric matrix has an orthonormal real eigenbasis and is orthogonally diagonalizable.

items.text: Diagonalizable means diagonalizable over a specified field: a real matrix can fail over R but succeed over C.
For each eigenvalue, geometric multiplicity is at most algebraic multiplicity; equality for every eigenvalue is equivalent to diagonalizability when the characteristic polynomial splits.
Repeated eigenvalues do not by themselves prevent diagonalization; too few independent eigenvectors do.
